# Decisions (muse)
- D1 (3 Nov, count corrected 6 Nov): Bonus claimed = **Best app with Atlassian MCP** (7 read-only `rovo:mcp` tools: slip added 3 Nov, portfolio exposed per D8, also used by the `rovo:agent`). Only one bonus can be won; Best Agents is eligible too but MCP has the stronger hosted evidence. Teamwork Graph is not claimed (allowlist ECOHELP-180616).
- D2 (3 Nov): Teamwork Graph provenance keeps `FULL`; `needsAdmin` and per-relation fields extend `coverage[]` (accepted with EXPERIENCE).
- D3 (3 Nov): Shared workspace stays a tested backend prototype until hosted two-account tests pass; private plans remain the default.
- D4 (3 Nov): Next differentiator = deterministic "what-if slip" simulation on Jira dates and dependencies (assumptions explicit, no invented probabilities).
- D5 (4 Nov): Wave 1 of the master mission = P0 storage-contract hardening + two P1 engine slices that are pure or unwired (low blast radius): portfolio simulator (simulation-core, not yet exposed via Forge) and workspace concurrency fix (still a PROTOTYPE, not wired). Forge exposure and UI come in wave 2 after review.
- D6 (4 Nov): Test store fakes enforce the Forge KVS key contract (`[a-zA-Z0-9:._ -#]`, <= 500 chars). The throttle wiring test now passes identity through the Forge runtime payload (it never did before, which is why the 2.31.0 outage was not caught); it fails on the pre-hotfix throttle.
- D7 (4 Nov): Throttle stays fail-open on storage errors (availability over abuse control): every operation still enforces its own Jira authorization, and the throttle only limits volume. Revisit if a hosted abuse case appears.
- D8 (4 Nov): Portfolio simulation is exposed (UI op `simulatePortfolio`, read-only Rovo action + MCP tool `anticipate-simulate-portfolio`, capability `portfolioSimulation`). Live snapshots stay capped at 200 nodes; the hash is stable for a reused `snapshotId`.
- D9 (4 Nov): Shared-decision ops are registered but refuse with UNSUPPORTED/FEATURE_DISABLED until `config:feature:sharedDecisions` is set by a site admin. Execution is not yet gated by `readyToExecute` (next step before enabling). Reason code `AWAITING_APPROVAL` added to the #131 enum.
- D10 (4 Nov): Decision radar (#132): feasible without new scopes via Forge triggers on issue-link created/deleted + issue deleted (events carry issue ids, delivery latency up to minutes, no documented ordering). First slice = mark plans NEEDS_REVIEW; checkPlanFreshness stays the source of truth before execution. Design: docs/design-core/DECISION_RADAR.md. Not built yet.
- D11 (4 Nov, owner; SUPERSEDED by D14 on 8 Nov — kept for history): Temporary single-orchestrator mode while orpheane is unavailable: muse may work on EXPERIENCE files (`static/hello-world`, UX copy, docs) as well as CORE, through its own `muse/*` branches and PRs merged on green CI. `state-orpheane.json` stays single-writer (orpheane only) and is not edited by muse; open orpheane branches/leases are not overwritten. Historical attribution is kept. The normal split resumes when orpheane is back.
- D12 (4 Nov, owner): K9 reclassified as an owner-accepted risk: the local bridge runs without HMAC by design (see risks.md K9). Agents do not restore HMAC on their own and do not block work on it; application and Atlassian permission boundaries are unchanged.
- D13 (7 Nov, owner via #95): Workflow-validator gate keeps latest-decision-wins discovery (`decision:{issueKey}` mirror, `src/main.ts validateTransition`): transition context carries only the issue key, single-plan-per-gated-change is the documented workflow (`docs/admin/WORKFLOW_VALIDATOR.md`), and records no longer clobber (#94), so the residual is confusion-only. Owner-scoped gating is deferred, not rejected: future prompt = designate the gating plan per issue (label value or issue property set at plan creation) and pass it as `expectedScope` through the ready validator API (`runValidator` already enforces owner+plan scope); add cross-owner e2e (two plans, one issue) before enabling.
- D14 (8 Nov, owner via coordination update): Normal two-agent organization restored. orpheane owns EXPERIENCE (static/hello-world, React UX, accessibility implementation, responsive polish, first-run usability) under TITAN-EXPERIENCE with active task leases. muse owns CORE, Forge, backend, security, MCP, production releases, commercial validation, official evidence, Devpost and submission compliance. muse does not modify EXPERIENCE-owned files while orpheane holds a lease; frontend needs go through GitHub issues + PR reviews. Independent branches, reviewable PRs, green CI each side; shared documentation stays CORE-owned.
